newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SUZUKI SEES FIRST-TIME PROFIT IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: SUZUKI SEES FIRST-TIME PROFIT IN HUNGARY.

text.p: The Hungarian plant of Japanese automaker Suzuki Motor Corp said on Wednesday it will post its first profit in 1996, with estimated pre-tax earnings of 750 million forints on revenue of 55 billion forints.
The plant, Magyar Suzuki Rt (MS), will release final results in April, its sales director Shinzo Nakanishi told Reuters.
"Last year was exciting because it was the first time we showed a profit," Nakanishi said, crediting the turnaround to increased car production to 51,000 units in 1996 from 36,000 units in 1995.
MS reported a loss of 600 million forints in 1995, 2.0 billion forints in 1994 and 6.2 billion forints in 1993. It started building cars in October 1992.
A rise in output to 55,000 units in 1997 should boost profits "a little" and revenue to 60 billion forints, Nakanishi said, declining to cite a specific earnings forecast.
MS, owned 77.7 percent by Suzuki, builds Suzuki Swift hatchbacks and sedans with engines and transmissions imported from Japan.
Roughly 15 percent of output in 1995 was produced with the model name Subaru Justy, a brand of Japanese conglomerate Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd , which sells the cars in European Union countries.

MS sold around 13,000 units of its output in Hungary last year, Nakanishi said. The main export markets were Britain, Germany and the Netherlands, but the company also is looking to export to South America, he added.
